subject: Post-demo follow-up: token runrate sketch & 99th TPS probe
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@fastledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: token runrate sketch & 99th TPS probe

Thanks again for your time today, Sam — helpful session. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size the hosted API proposal and check SLA tolerance: 

1) Monthly expected token range (user-facing generation + embeddings): you mentioned a steady base plus growth -- can you confirm the target band we should model? Options you referenced: 
   - Conservative: 12M tokens / month
   - Typical: 40M tokens / month
   - Aggressive: 140M tokens / month

2) Peak concurrency / 99th percentile TPS: you said some spikes hit short windows during end-of-minute ingest. Can you confirm the 99th percentile TPS you want us to guarantee for production? You gave an example of ~380 TPS during demo peak; we need a formal number to size reserved capacity.

3) Target price $/1M tokens (ballpark): do you have an internal target bandwidth for hosted-cost planning? We typically present tiered options but we can tailor the first-pass quote to a $/1M anchor if you have a target.

Next steps from our side: I'll attach a one-page mutual action plan and a small sample-traffic CSV template you can drop your traffic into (will use to simulate KV/cache hit rates and batching efficiency). If you can fill the CSV for a representative week, we can run a quick cost/latency sensitivity and share a proposal.

Deliverables we’ll produce after the CSV: a) a 2-option hosted plan with $/1M anchor and expected monthly spend at each token band, b) a peak-capacity sizing note with 99th TPS recommendation and fallback model mapping.

Can we aim to get the sample CSV back by EOD Wed (Dec 2)? That would let us share the first proposal on Thursday.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (outline), sample_traffic_week.csv (template)

From: Sam Park <sam.park@fastledger.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@fastledger.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: token runrate sketch & 99th TPS probe

Appreciate the recap, Aditya. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly token bands: those three are right directionally. For internal approvals we want the proposal to model both Typical (40M) and Aggressive (140M). The Conservative band (12M) is still useful but likely underestimates our roadmap.

- 99th TPS: we measured a short-lived burst that hit ~420 TPS for ~25s during a user import flow. Real-world steady-state 99th is closer to 180-220 TPS, but we want the platform to tolerate the 420 TPS microburst without throttling critical paths. If you can present options that cover 220 TPS (tight), and a hardened 420 TPS (burst tolerant) that would be ideal.

- Target $/1M: procurement gave a range of $75–$200 per 1M tokens depending on latency/SLA commitment. If you can show a pricing ladder that maps to 220 TPS vs 420 TPS commitments, that would align well.

We can populate the sample CSV — I’ll have Emma drop a cleaned week by EOD Wed. 

Thanks,
Sam Park
Head of Platform Engineering | FastLedger
sam.park@fastledger.com

Perfect, Sam — that helps a lot. Couple of clarifying datapoints from our side so the proposal is practical: 

- When you say "420 TPS for ~25s", can you confirm whether that was compositionally (a) small idempotent single-token evals, (b) multi-token generation calls ~200–400 tokens, or (c) a mixed batch? The cost and KV cache behavior differs across those.

- For pricing ladder: we typically show three anchored options: 
  * Standard (no SLA): best-effort, suitable for dev/test or non-critical prod (lower $/1M)
  * Business (SLA 99.9 latency/availability, 220 TPS sizing): middle band
  * Enterprise (SLA + burst buffer to 420 TPS, dedicated capacity / reserved): top band

Marissa — looping you in for pricing input. Ben — can you run a quick modeling pass on batching efficiency if FastLedger returns the sample CSV? I’ve attached the MAP and the CSV template.

Action items:
- Sam/Emma: return sample_traffic_week.csv (representative week) by EOD Wed, Dec 2
- Ben: run batching + KV-cache sim on returned CSV and return efficiency estimate (percent token reduction) by Thurs morning
- Marissa: prepare 3-option price ladder with $/1M anchors mapping to token bands and TPS commitments by Thurs COB

Thanks —
Aditya
Aditya Rao | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the detail here — jumping in on pricing. High-level guidance for the proposal: 

- Price anchors we recommend presenting (USD per 1M tokens):
  • Standard: $65 / 1M (best-effort; no guaranteed 99th TPS)
  • Business: $125 / 1M (guaranteed sizing to 220 TPS, 99.9 latency SLOs)
  • Enterprise: $195 / 1M (dedicated reserved capacity + burst headroom to 420 TPS; includes extended observability retention)

- For the 40M vs 140M bands, we’ll show expected monthly spend and a blended discount for committed monthly units. Example (illustrative): 
  • 40M tokens: Standard = $2,600/mo; Business = $5,000/mo; Enterprise = $7,800/mo
  • 140M tokens: Standard = $9,100/mo; Business = $17,500/mo; Enterprise = $27,300/mo

- Note on economics: caching and batching materially reduce effective token spend — if Ben’s sim shows >20% effective token reduction at typical interaction shapes, we’ll surface a second column that shows "net unit spend" after cache/hit savings.

I’ll slot time Thurs afternoon for a quick internal alignment and will upload the first draft pricing spreadsheet to the drive link once Ben’s simulation numbers land.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
